scope: Foundation class-by-class method port: List, Sequence, AliasedArray, ForwardRange, UtfIterator; typed allocator provenance repair
integration_status: uncommitted main working-tree drafts; .git is read-only

remaining_partial_contracts: Mutable iterator conversions and writable const aliases need a separate unsafe compatibility interface.
Rust drops allocated values on failure; native failure paths may leak nodes. Exact constructor/destructor/allocator hook equivalence remains partial.
Prefix/postfix and arrow wrappers over private native BasicIterator require a compiler-visible public-alias reachability proof before API credit.
Negative self-insertion overloads and checked endpoint exception wrappers remain to be completed.
Native node layout, arbitrary C++ copy/move hooks and mutable iterator aliasing remain partial.
Rust Iterator is a safe traversal adapter; native private iterator increment/decrement declarations still require public-alias reachability proof.

Native Move and move construction leave the source as a non-owning alias with unchanged pointer/range. Safe Rust move_from empties the source. The oracle records native-source-alias separately; this difference is not approved as parity.
Only the default 16-byte native alignment policy is represented; MyAlignSize template policies remain unported.
Native const external pointers may be written through a cast; safe Rust only accepts an exclusive mutable slice, and signed prefix construction checks that the slice is long enough.
Typed APIs accept ArrayValue/Pod types only; arbitrary C++ object representations, assignment hooks, overlapping writable aliases, and unaligned reference access are not claimed.

Rust fresh allocation zeroes bytes and checks byte-count overflow; native fresh bytes are indeterminate and native stride narrowing can truncate a size_t larger than UINT32_MAX. Existing Rust checked_stride rejects those strides.

Allocator hook policy and out-of-memory behavior are not equivalent. Native discard-resize frees owned storage before allocation; existing Rust resize allocates replacement storage before dropping the old block.
No new integrated API or original declaration mapping credit; candidate bindings need compiler-backed symbol capture and final integration validation.
Accessor selection remains explicit Rust descriptors rather than automatic C++ method-name detection.
Safe current/postfix stop at exhaustion; pre_increment is the exact unconditional native prefix delegation.

Mutable internal cursor references and independently copied adapters over an exclusive external host are not represented. Rust references returned by accessors must have lifetimes independent of the short host borrow.
ChangeBufferHere writable aliases are not implemented for shared input slices.
Input slices synthesize zero padding at exhaustion; pointer getters do not turn this padding into dereferenceable storage.
Null increment panics instead of native undefined null dereference.
Signed char template/overload variants and platform-specific wchar_t ABI are not independently proven.

allocator_repair.reason: Box can return a reborrowed payload pointer without access to the hidden allocation prefix. Typed heap allocation now reconstructs its layout from the Allocator API, avoiding out-of-bounds provenance access.
allocator_repair.limitations: Typed heap allocations use the exact requested Rust payload layout, with policy minimum alignment; raw OCCT byte allocations retain their native rounding/header behavior. Native allocator hooks and exact allocation-failure parity remain unproven.
